evidence.craft: Read hv.py (27 lines), proposers.py (186), screen.py (103), bench.py (56), space.py (36), tests/test_screen.py (75), experiments/run.py, figure.py. Code is short and readable, but hv.py, proposers.py, space.py are byte-identical copies of eda-screen's (and screen.py/bench.py copies plus a few lines), i.e. a third copy of the same engine rather than an import; proposers.py carries four proposers (Grid, Annealing, Genetic, NSGA2) never used here; two dominance helpers with opposite argument order (hv.dominated(a,b) means b dominates a; screen.dominates(a,b) means a dominates b), an easy future bug; figure.py docstring names screen_hv.svg but writes cheapaware_hv.svg; run.py writes into the committed results.txt with no output flag.
evidence.claims: Checked: '0.901 at 12', '0.860 random', '0.878 TPE', '0.990 screen k=4', '+0.041 / 74% of paired seeds', '87% of seeds by 20', 'none of the seeds even at 30', table rows 4-30: all backed by experiments/results.txt and reproduced. 'Stylised and preliminary' label and limitations present. Unbacked or misleading: 'the cell-count surrogate is worth the other +0.089' (README:8) attributes the remainder to the fitted surrogate, but a zero-synthesis designer prior (cells proportional to p x wb, fast 10% larger), ranked by the same non-dominated sorting with random ties, reaches 0.978 at 12 and the whole front on 100% of draws at 20 (/tmp/claude-0/audit-eda-cheapaware/proxy.py), so about +0.077 of the +0.089 needs no syntheses or model at all; the limitation 'relative to it' does not tell a reader that. Layer prose error noted under correctness.
evidence.fitness: A researcher could build on the harness (fast, deterministic, reproducible) but not on the conclusion. Nearest prior work: multi-objective optimisation with heterogeneous objective evaluation costs (Allmendinger, Handl and Knowles 2015, 'Multiobjective optimization: when objectives exhibit non-uniform latencies', EJOR 243(2):497; Chugh et al. 2018 on heterogeneous objectives in surrogate-assisted EAs; Wang et al. 2022 on transfer-learning heterogeneous objectives) and learning-based HLS DSE (Liu and Carloni 2013, DAC). None is cited; exploiting cheap objectives first is the standard move in that literature, so the result is an ablation on one 80-point space rather than a new finding. Sound within its stated limits, but the missing monotone-prior baseline changes the reading of its headline split.
evidence.domain: Against DSE practice: equal-synthesis budget accounting, exact hypervolume with a fixed reference, 100 paired seeds and bootstrap intervals are fine. Departures: no PPA-aware prior baseline (an EDA designer knows area scales with lanes x bit width before any synthesis; this is the first baseline a reviewer asks for); a single 80-design space where the cheap objectives depend only on (p, wb), so the two ABC scripts always tie; degenerate bootstrap intervals (0.901 to 0.901) reported as 95% intervals without saying the quantity is deterministic at that budget; generic-gate cell count, no place and route (stated).

defects.what: Headline attributes the remaining +0.089 of the screen's lead to 'the cell-count surrogate', but no PPA-aware prior baseline was run: a zero-synthesis designer prior (cells proportional to lanes x width) with the same ranking reaches 0.978 at 12 and the whole front at 20, so roughly +0.077 of the +0.089 needs no fitted model; the decomposition is baseline-dependent and the README reads as if it were not.

Hypervolume, the metric every number rests on, has no known-value test: changing the 1-D base case to ref-max leaves all tests green (the oracle test checks only a ratio of two equally wrong volumes).
CheapRandom's uniform draw within a layer (the new method's only stochastic step) is untested: replacing it by layer[0] leaves all tests green.

README explains the plateau as one free-objective Pareto layer exhausted by 12; the layers are 2, 10, 12, ... designs, so it is two layers, and the stall runs through syntheses 13-24 (all of layer 3), not 'until 20'.

Nearest prior work on multi-objective optimisation with heterogeneous objective costs (Allmendinger, Handl and Knowles 2015, EJOR; Chugh et al. 2018) and learning-based HLS DSE (Liu and Carloni 2013) not cited; novelty of 'use the free objectives first' not positioned.

hv.py, proposers.py, space.py copied byte-for-byte from eda-screen (third copy of the engine), four unused proposers carried along, and two dominance helpers with opposite argument order (hv.dominated vs screen.dominates).
figure.py docstring says it writes experiments/screen_hv.svg; it writes cheapaware_hv.svg.

verdict: Numbers are right: results.txt reruns byte-identically and an independent hypervolume and cheap-aware-random simulation reproduce the table (0.901 at 12, 0.933 at 30, 12-point true front). It does not meet the bar: 3 of 5 seeded mutants survive (including the hypervolume itself), and the headline split '+0.041 free objectives, +0.089 surrogate' omits the baseline a DSE reviewer asks for first: a zero-synthesis 'cells grow with lanes x width' prior reaches 0.978 at 12 and the full front at 20, so most of the surrogate's credited share is available without any model. Prior work on heterogeneous-cost multi-objective optimisation is not cited.
